Location: Germany (On-site / Hybrid with Relocation & Housing Support)

Working Language: English (No initial German language skills required) 

About the Research Institute: 

The IRIS Institute (gGmbH) bridges the gap between scientific spatial data research and practical implementation, identifying and evaluating high-value strategic sites for energy storage systems and digital infrastructure. 

What We Offer: 

We provide complete end-to-end support for international candidates under the German Opportunity Card system, including official paperwork, degree validation, housing assistance, and living allowances during the trainee phase. On-site German language courses and direct involvement in high-impact energy infrastructure initiatives are part of the package. 

Your Role & Key Tasks: 

You will translate spatial data analyses and infrastructure parameters into structured location dossiers and automated B2B lead profiles. You will support technical communications with project partners and institutional stakeholders, while capturing practical industry feedback to continuously refine our spatial queries and research algorithms. 

Candidate Profile & Qualifications: 

Applicants should possess a completed degree in Business Engineering, Spatial Economics, Real Estate, Spatial Planning, or Geoinformatics with a commercial mindset. You must have strong communication and organizational skills, an ability to interpret infrastructure maps and site metrics, and fluent English skills. 

How to Apply: 

Please submit your CV and a short cover letter in English. We look forward to welcoming you to our initiative! Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter in English directly to: 

jobs@iris-institut.info (https://mailto:jobs@iris-institut.info)

Location: Germany (On-site / Hybrid with Relocation & Housing Support) 

Target Program: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) / Master Trainees / International Talents 

Working Language: English (No initial German language skills required) 

About the Research Institute: 

The IRIS Institute (gGmbH) is a non-profit, applied research institute dedicated to developing cutting-edge spatial resilience data models and open-data architectures for the energy transition, critical infrastructure, and sustainable regional planning. 

What We Offer: 

We provide comprehensive administrative support for international candidates, including full assistance with the German Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte), degree recognition, and visa procedures. You will receive structured onboarding, local accommodation support, coverage of basic living expenses during training, on-site sponsored German language courses, and access to a modern data engineering tech stack centered on Python, PostGIS, Docker, and GIS platforms. 

Your Role & Key Tasks: 

In this role, you will build and maintain automated Python-based spatial data pipelines connecting to WFS services, REST APIs, and public open-data platforms. You will implement spatial overlay and inference models for energy grid matching and land-use analysis, while validating, structuring, and transforming vector geometries into our central PostgreSQL and PostGIS databases. 

Candidate Profile & Qualifications: 

We welcome applicants with a completed university degree in Geoinformatics, Computer Science, Data Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related technical discipline. You should bring practical experience or a strong learning interest in Python (GeoPandas, Shapely), SQL databases (PostgreSQL/PostGIS), spatial reference systems, and automated data ingestion workflows. High motivation and fluent English skills are required. 

How to Apply: 

Please submit your CV along with a short cover letter in English. We look forward to welcoming you to the IRIS team! jobs@iris-institut.info (https://mailto:jobs@iris-institut.info)

About ForEveryone ForEveryone is a non-profit social enterprise in Berlin. We bring people from different backgrounds together, among other things through our community café at Boxhagener Platz and through workshops, events and activities for an international Berlin audience. We are growing, and we are currently reshaping our whole range of activities.

What this role is about We are looking for someone to oversee, develop and be present across our whole range of activities – from workshops to events at our community café at Boxhagener Platz (jam sessions, music nights, exhibitions and more). The clear goal: turning individual activities into recurring small communities with their own memberships. Instead of activities we have to market and fill again every time, we want formats people come back to regularly – a knitting club, a sports format, creative combinations, a recurring music night. You drive this: you sense what the community wants, develop formats to match, test them, run them yourself, recruit and support the volunteers who help carry them, and make sure the good ones actually happen and grow.

What you'll do

- Oversee and support the offering. You keep an eye on all running activities – workshops and café events alike – are regularly present on site, and make sure everything runs smoothly, including the operational side in our booking tool (cancellations, refunds, correct details) – a small but important part of the week.
- Develop and test formats and events. You sense what activities the community wants, identify new workshop, event and mini-formats, research trends and seasonal demand (what are others offering, what works in a summer lull?), and honestly test which formats land well enough to sustain, and which don't.
- Build mini-communities with memberships. You develop formats with recurring communities in mind – ones people belong to as members – and take them from first idea to an established, recurring offering.
- Run activities and enable volunteers. You run workshops and events yourself on a regular basis, at a good standard – weekly, sometimes with support from volunteers. You recruit volunteers (including from among participants), onboard them, give them direct feedback, and support them until they can carry a format.
- Guide formats through their phases. For new formats: experiment and learn from feedback. For established ones: set up clean processes, with reliability and scaling in mind.

What you bring

- Experience running workshops, events, groups or community formats, at a quality others can build on.
- A feel for people and communities, and enjoyment in recruiting and supporting volunteers.
- Conceptual strength: you can develop formats, test them, and judge honestly what works.
- Self-direction and ownership – you drive your area like a genuine project lead.
- Fixed on-site times: at least 3–4 evenings per week (around 2–3 hours each, within the 5–10 pm window) plus 1 day at the weekend (Saturday or Sunday, daytime or evening). These are your core working hours. The rest of your time you can arrange flexibly from the office. This on-site presence comes with a lot of creative freedom, but it is also a clear expectation.
- Comfortable with digital tools; German and English are a strong plus for our multilingual community.

What to expect from us

- A role with real room to shape things: you are building something that doesn't exist yet.
- A small, committed team and real closeness to a lively, international community.
- We set the strategic and financial direction (e.g. the membership model) as managing directors; you develop and decide on the formats independently, with our final sign-off.

Terms

- Hours: 32–36 per week
- Start: September/October 2026 or by arrangement
- Pay: €2,400–2,800 gross/month (at 36 hrs)
- Location: Coworking Kiezlab, Berlin · hybrid
